I am 68 years old and have farmed in Quzhou County for decades. I have 7 mu of good flat land on the North China Plain. My children have left for the city, so I manage the fields mostly by myself, hiring a machine operator at sowing and harvest. Because I finished more schooling than most of my neighbors, I read the county extension bulletins and understand the value of improved varieties, but at my age I do not take big risks with untested crops. This year, like most years, I will stick to the wheat-maize rotation that has always fed my family and given me a steady income.

My winter wheat is already in the ground from last October — I planted an improved semi-dwarf variety that resists lodging. Now that spring has arrived, I will topdress with nitrogen at green-up and again at jointing, irrigate three times, and spray for weeds, aphids, and powdery mildew. After harvesting the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant a hybrid maize variety using no-tillage direct seeding into the wheat stubble. There is no time to waste between crops. For the maize, I will apply compound fertilizer at sowing and topdress at the big-flare stage, irrigate twice, and control weeds and corn borers. I do not grow cotton or vegetables anymore — my back cannot handle the bending and extra labor, and grain crops give me reliable returns with less risk.
